```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os, re
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import pandas as pd

DOC = "PCMP-001"
UO = None
UO_TITLE = "A-Mab Drug Substance"

# --- revision and campaign facts ---
ver, eff = doc_version(DOC)
rev1_ver, rev1_eff = REV1["rev"], rev1_date(DOC)
pkg_rev1 = REV1["effective"]          # Version 1.0 approval of the reports and PCMR-001

inv_id, inv_open, inv_close, inv_class = INV["id"], INV["opened"], INV["closed"], INV["classification"]
amd_id, amd_date = AMD["id"], AMD["date"]

def g(x):
    return f"{float(x):g}"

# --- the two sites, as the title block names them ---
dev_site, com_site = (re.sub(r"\s*\(.*\)$", "", s.replace(f"{COMPANY} — ", "")) for s in (SENDING_SITE, RECEIVING_SITE))
_tb = title_block(DOC, UO_TITLE)
assert re.search(rf"\|\s*Development site\s*\|\s*{re.escape(dev_site)}\s*\|", _tb)
assert re.search(rf"\|\s*Commercial drug substance site\s*\|\s*{re.escape(com_site)}\s*\|", _tb)

# --- train and scope ---
steps = list(CFG.train_order)
n_steps = len(steps)
first_title = UNIT_OP_TITLES[steps[0]]
last_title = UNIT_OP_TITLES[steps[-1]]
first_step, last_step = CFG.unit_op(steps[0]).step, CFG.unit_op(steps[-1]).step
doe_keys = [k for k in steps if os.path.exists(os.path.join(DATA, f"doe_{k}_rsm.csv"))]
nodoe_keys = [k for k in steps if k not in doe_keys]
n_doe = len(doe_keys)
SHORT = {"harvest": "harvest", "ufdf": "UF/DF"}
nodoe_names = " and ".join(f"{SHORT.get(k, UNIT_OP_TITLES[k].lower())} (Step {CFG.unit_op(k).step})" for k in nodoe_keys)
n_ppq = V["n_ppq"]

# --- CQA register ---
cqa_tab = all_cqas().copy()
cqa_tab["Formed or set at"] = [UNIT_OP_TITLES[s] for s in cqa_reg["set_by"]]
n_cqa = len(cqa_tab)
vl_names = " and ".join(c[0].lower() + c[1:] for c in cqa_reg.loc[cqa_reg.criticality == "VL", "cqa"])
def join_and(xs):
    xs = list(xs)
    return xs[0] if len(xs) == 1 else ", ".join(xs[:-1]) + " and " + xs[-1]
def pname(n):
    return n[0].lower() + n[1:]
_p = param_reg
_both = _p[(_p.par_low < _p.nor_low) & (_p.par_high > _p.nor_high)]
_eq = _p[(_p.par_low == _p.nor_low) & (_p.par_high == _p.nor_high)]
_one = _p[~_p.index.isin(_both.index) & ~_p.index.isin(_eq.index)]
n_wide_both, n_one_end, n_equal = len(_both), len(_one), len(_eq)
one_end_names = join_and(pname(n) for n in _one.parameter)
equal_names = join_and(n for n in _eq.parameter)
_bio = _p[_p.step == CFG.unit_op("bioreactor").step]
bio_mv = join_and(pname(n) for n in _bio[_bio.study == "multivariate"].parameter)
bio_uv = join_and(pname(n) for n in _bio[_bio.study != "multivariate"].parameter)

# --- risk basis ---
scope = char_scope_df()
n_par = int(scope["Parameters"].sum())
n_mv = int(scope["Multivariate"].sum())
n_uv = int(scope["Univariate"].sum())
n_nodoe_par = int(scope.loc[scope["Multivariate"] == 0, "Parameters"].sum())

# --- scale-down models: equipment, holds ---
chrono = csv("study_chronology.csv")
# the plan lists its campaign: the studies the Version 1.0 reports analysed, and the supplementary
# qualification study of the Protein A scale-down model (PD-005-01). The other studies of the Version 2.0
# re-analysis (the INV-002 augmentations, the support of the re-centred low-pH set-points, the osmolality
# study and the new univariate studies of harvest and UF/DF) are reported by the reports of their steps
chrono = chrono[(chrono["start"] < pkg_rev1) | (chrono["kind"] == "qualification")].reset_index(drop=True)
eq = equipment_df()
eq_used = chrono.dropna(subset=["equipment"]).merge(eq, left_on="equipment", right_on="Equipment")
eq_used["ok"] = eq_used["end"] < eq_used["Next calibration due"]
eq_tab = pd.DataFrame({
    "Equipment": eq_used["equipment"],
    "Description": eq_used["Description"],
    "Study": eq_used["id"],
    "Study window": eq_used["start"] + " to " + eq_used["end"],
    "Next calibration due": eq_used["Next calibration due"],
})
eq_all_ok = bool(eq_used["ok"].all())
n_eq = eq_used["equipment"].nunique()          # the systems the studies of the campaign used
last_end = chrono["end"].max()
all_before_rev1 = bool((chrono["end"] < pkg_rev1).all())
plan_before_studies = bool(rev1_eff < chrono["start"].min())
_pre = chrono[chrono["end"] < pkg_rev1]
_post = chrono[chrono["end"] >= pkg_rev1]
pre_last_end = _pre["end"].max()
# the qualification runs of each step closed before its first characterization run (§5, §7.1)
for _r in chrono[(chrono["kind"] == "qualification") & (chrono["start"] < pkg_rev1)].itertuples():
    _later = chrono[(chrono["step"] == _r.step) & (chrono["kind"] != "qualification")]
    assert _later.empty or _r.end < _later["start"].min(), _r.id
post_ids = ", ".join(_post["id"])
post_window = "; ".join(f"{r.start} to {r.end}" for r in _post.itertuples())
holds = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["holds"]
def hold_temps(k):
    t = holds[k]["temps"]
    return f"{t[0]} and {t[1]}"
hold_days = max(max(h["days"]) for h in holds.values())
n_hold_temps = len(holds["harvest"]["temps"])
# the hold studies were made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after the Version 1.0 reports, and each
# report records its own as a discrepancy from its plan; no plan describes one (owner, 2026-10-09)
_hold_ids = [h["study"] for h in holds.values()]
_hold_pd = {x for ds in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES.values() for d in ds for x in d.get("studies", [])}
assert set(_hold_ids) <= _hold_pd
_hc = csv("study_chronology.csv").set_index("id").loc[_hold_ids]
assert bool((_hc["start"] > REV1["effective"]).all())
hold_from, hold_to = _hc["start"].min(), _hc["end"].max()

# --- statistics ---
def resp_names(k):
    rs = list(D.responses(k)) + [r for r in D.fragment_responses(k, "rsm") if r == "lmw_cesds_pct"]
    return ", ".join(D.RESP_LABEL.get(r, r) for r in rs)
def scr_terms(k):
    n = len(D.screening_factors(k))
    return 1 + n + n * (n - 1) // 2
design_tab = pd.DataFrame([{
    "Step": CFG.unit_op(k).step,
    "Unit operation": UNIT_OP_TITLES[k].replace(" Chromatography", ""),
    "Scr. factors": len(D.screening_factors(k)),
    "Scr. runs": f"{doe_runs(k, 'screening')} ({doe_centre_points(k, 'screening')})",
    "Scr. model terms": scr_terms(k),
    "RSM factors": len(D.rsm_factors(k)),
    "RSM runs": f"{doe_runs(k, 'rsm')} ({doe_centre_points(k, 'rsm')})",
    "Responses": resp_names(k),
} for k in doe_keys])
min_cp = min(min(doe_centre_points(k, "screening"), doe_centre_points(k, "rsm")) for k in doe_keys)
n_mc = V["n_monte_carlo"]
par_mc, par_grid = D.PAR_MC_N, D.PAR_GRID
# screening designs whose interaction model leaves no residual beyond the centre points
def lof_df(k):
    return doe_runs(k, "screening") - scr_terms(k) - (doe_centre_points(k, "screening") - 1)
sat_keys = [k for k in doe_keys if lof_df(k) <= 1]
sat_lof = max(lof_df(k) for k in sat_keys)
sat_names = " and ".join(UNIT_OP_TITLES[k].lower() for k in sat_keys)
sat_k = {k: len(D.screening_factors(k)) for k in sat_keys}
# campaign thresholds (PCMP-001 Version 2.0)
cpk_target, cpk_min = g(CPK_TARGET), g(CPK_MIN)
lof_alpha = g(THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"])
max_gap = f"{THRESHOLDS['max_r2_minus_pred_r2']:.2f}"

# --- intermediate acceptance criteria ---
iac = D.iac_table()
def iac_row(step, cqa):
    return iac[(iac.step_key == step) & (iac.cqa == cqa)].iloc[0]
r_brx_agg = iac_row("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw")
r_vi_agg = iac_row("viral_inactivation", "aggregates_hmw")
r_cex_agg = iac_row("cex", "aggregates_hmw")
r_pa_hcp = iac_row("protein_a", "hcp")
r_cex_hcp = iac_row("cex", "hcp")
pa_hcp_fold = T.num(r_pa_hcp["downstream_fold"])
pa_hcp_iac = T.num(r_pa_hcp["iac_high"])
cex_hcp_fold = T.num(r_cex_hcp["downstream_fold"])
_plat = CFG.raw()["iac"]["platform"]
plat_cex_hcp, plat_aex_hcp = g(_plat["cex"]["hcp"]["fold_min"]), g(_plat["aex"]["hcp"]["fold_min"])
pa_hcp_apriori, cex_hcp_apriori = T.num(r_pa_hcp["iac_high_apriori"]), T.num(r_cex_hcp["iac_high_apriori"])
cex_hcp_iac = T.num(r_cex_hcp["iac_high"])
assert bool(r_pa_hcp["widened"])
assert abs(float(r_pa_hcp["iac_high_apriori"]) - float(r_pa_hcp["ds_high"]) * _plat["cex"]["hcp"]["fold_min"] * _plat["aex"]["hcp"]["fold_min"]) < 1e-6
ds_hcp = T.num(r_pa_hcp["ds_high"])
n_iac = len(iac)
n_iac_steps = iac["step_key"].nunique()
n_tight = int(iac["tightened"].astype(bool).sum())
brx_agg_apriori, brx_agg_now = T.num(r_brx_agg["iac_high_apriori"]), T.num(r_brx_agg["iac_high"])
vi_agg_apriori, vi_agg_now = T.num(r_vi_agg["iac_high_apriori"]), T.num(r_vi_agg["iac_high"])
cex_agg_iac = g(r_cex_agg["iac_high"])

claims = CFG.raw()["iac"]["viral_claims"]
vcum = csv("iac_viral_cumulative.csv")
vc_tab = pd.DataFrame([{
    "Virus": {"lrv_xmulv": "XMuLV (enveloped)", "lrv_mvm": "MVM (parvovirus)"}[r.cqa],
    "Low-pH viral inactivation": g(claims["viral_inactivation"].get({"lrv_xmulv": "xmulv_lrf", "lrv_mvm": "mvm_lrf"}[r.cqa], float("nan"))) if {"lrv_xmulv": "xmulv_lrf", "lrv_mvm": "mvm_lrf"}[r.cqa] in claims["viral_inactivation"] else "no claim",
    "Anion exchange": g(claims["aex"][{"lrv_xmulv": "xmulv_lrf", "lrv_mvm": "mvm_lrf"}[r.cqa]]),
    "Virus filtration": g(claims["virus_filtration"][{"lrv_xmulv": "xmulv_lrf", "lrv_mvm": "mvm_lrf"}[r.cqa]]),
    "Sum of claims": f"{r.claimed_sum:.2f}",
    "Cumulative requirement": g(r.required),
    "Met": "yes" if bool(r.met) else "no",
} for r in vcum.itertuples()])
vc_all_met = bool(vcum["met"].astype(bool).all())
xm = vcum[vcum.cqa == "lrv_xmulv"].iloc[0]
mv = vcum[vcum.cqa == "lrv_mvm"].iloc[0]

# --- verification ---
verif = D.iac_verification()
n_verif = len(verif)
n_verif_testable = int(verif["met"].notna().sum())
n_verif_untestable = n_verif - n_verif_testable
n_verif_failed = int((verif["met"] == 0).sum())
n_verif_met = int((verif["met"] == 1).sum())
v_cex_agg = verif[(verif.step_key == "cex") & (verif.cqa == "aggregates_hmw")].iloc[0]
cex_agg_assumed = T.num(v_cex_agg["assumed"])
cex_agg_pred = T.num(v_cex_agg["predicted_nor"])

# --- Version 1.0 example (cation exchange pool aggregate) ---
r1 = D.rev1_criteria("cex")
r1_cex_agg = r1[r1.cqa == "aggregates_hmw"].iloc[0]
r1_cex_agg_hi, r1_cex_agg_margin = g(r1_cex_agg["high"]), g(r1_cex_agg["margin"])
ds_agg = g(cqa_reg.loc[cqa_reg.key == "aggregates_hmw", "acc_high"].iloc[0])

# --- methods ---
st = {s["id"]: s for s in CFG.raw()["campaign"]["studies"]}
pa_ret_start, pa_ret_end = st["S-PA-RET"]["start"], st["S-PA-RET"]["end"]
frc_start, frc_end = st["S-CEX-FRC"]["start"], st["S-CEX-FRC"]["end"]
cesds_amv = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["cesds"]["id"]
cesds_sop = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["cesds"]["sop"]
sec_amv = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["sec"]["id"]

# --- capability ---
acid = cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == "acidic_variants"].iloc[0]
acid_lo, acid_hi = g(acid["acc_low"]), g(acid["acc_high"])

# --- classification counts ---
cc = class_counts()

# --- register of plans and schedule ---
plan_tab = pd.DataFrame([{
    "Plan": f"PCP-{CFG.unit_op(k).step:03d}",
    "Subject": DOC_REGISTRY[f"PCP-{CFG.unit_op(k).step:03d}"][1],
    "Study type": "screening and response surface" if k in doe_keys else "univariate and qualitative",
    "Paired report": f"PCR-{CFG.unit_op(k).step:03d}",
} for k in steps])
KIND = {"screening": "screening design", "rsm": "response-surface design", "univariate": "univariate",
        "hold": "hold study", "comparability": "method comparability", "superseded": "first execution (invalidated)",
        "retest": "retest of retained samples", "qualification": "scale-down model qualification"}
chrono_tab = pd.DataFrame({
    "Study": chrono["id"],
    "Step": [UNIT_OP_TITLES[s] for s in chrono["step"]],
    "Study type": [KIND.get(k, k) for k in chrono["kind"]],
    "Start": chrono["start"],
    "End": chrono["end"],
}).sort_values(["Start", "Study"]).reset_index(drop=True)
first_start = chrono["start"].min()
n_studies = len(chrono)
# some studies overlap in time (steps studied in parallel)
_c = chrono.sort_values("start").reset_index(drop=True)
assert any(_c.loc[i, "start"] <= _c.loc[:i - 1, "end"].max() for i in range(1, len(_c)))

# --- thresholds (Version 2.0) ---
effect_alpha = g(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
assert CPK_MIN == 1.0          # "at that value the process spread just reaches the criterion"

# --- scale-down offsets (owner's decision 2026-10-08): rule only, no offsets reported here ---
offset_ci = f"{100 * float(CFG.raw()['analytics']['sdm']['offset_ci']):g}"
assert CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"].get("apply_offset", False)
# viral clearance and fragments have no qualification data, so carry no offset
assert all(D.sdm_offset(k, r) is None for k in doe_keys for r in D.responses(k) if r.endswith("_lrf"))
assert all(D.sdm_offset(k, "lmw_cesds_pct") is None for k in doe_keys)
# step yield is an output with no criterion: offset recorded, nothing judged
assert all(D.effective_acceptance(k, "step_yield") is None for k in doe_keys if "step_yield" in D.responses(k))

# --- supplementary qualification study after Version 1.0, recorded as a discrepancy from the plan ---
assert len(_post) == 1
post_id = _post["id"].iloc[0]
pd_rec = [d for ds in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES.values() for d in ds if post_id in d.get("studies", [])][0]
pd_id, pd_plan, pd_reason = pd_rec["id"], pd_rec["plan"], pd_rec["reason"]
pd_report = [r for r, ds in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES.items() if pd_rec in ds][0]
assert inv_open <= _post["start"].iloc[0] and _post["end"].iloc[0] <= inv_close

# --- decision statistic per attribute class ---
assert all(D.decision_statistic(r) == "worst_case" for r in ("xmulv_lrf", "mvm_lrf"))
assert D.decision_statistic("pool_hcp_ng_mg") == "batch"

# --- criteria in force: tightened and widened rows, computed from iac.csv ---
CQA_WORD = {"hcp": "host cell protein", "aggregates_hmw": "aggregate", "fragments_lmw": "fragments",
            "acidic_variants": "acidic variants", "leached_protein_a": "leached Protein A"}
UNIT = {"hcp": " ng/mg"}
POOL = {"bioreactor": "production bioreactor harvest", "protein_a": "Protein A pool",
        "viral_inactivation": "viral inactivation pool", "cex": "cation exchange pool",
        "aex": "anion exchange pool"}
def _crit_phrase(r):
    u = UNIT.get(r.cqa, " %")
    lim = "the upper limit for " if r.spec_type == "two_sided" else "the criterion for "
    return (f"{lim}{CQA_WORD[r.cqa]} in the {POOL[r.step_key]} "
            f"(from {T.num(r.iac_high_apriori)}{u} to {T.num(r.iac_high)}{u})")
_T, _W = iac["tightened"].astype(bool), iac["widened"].astype(bool)
_tight, _wide = iac[_T], iac[_W]
_tonly, _wonly, _both = iac[_T & ~_W], iac[_W & ~_T], iac[_T & _W]
n_tight, n_wide, n_both = len(_tight), len(_wide), len(_both)
n_moved = int((_T | _W).sum())
n_apriori = n_iac - n_moved
assert n_tight > 0 and len(_wonly) > 0 and n_both == 1
assert (_tonly["iac_high"] < _tonly["iac_high_apriori"]).all()          # each tightened-only is stricter
assert (_wonly["iac_high"] > _wonly["iac_high_apriori"]).all()          # each widened-only is wider
assert (_wide["iac_low"] == _wide["iac_low_apriori"]).all()
assert set(_tight["cqa"]) == {"aggregates_hmw"}                         # "the aggregate criteria"
assert all(steps.index(k) < steps.index("cex") for k in _tight["step_key"])   # upstream of CEX
_vcexagg = verif[(verif.step_key == "cex") & (verif.cqa == "aggregates_hmw")].iloc[0]
# tightening uses the single-batch prediction bound of the CEX aggregate clearance, not the point prediction
assert all(abs(_tight["downstream_fold"] - float(_vcexagg["predicted_nor_bound95"])) < 1e-3)
both = _both.iloc[0]
assert both.step_key == "bioreactor" and both.cqa == "aggregates_hmw"
_vviagg = verif[(verif.step_key == "viral_inactivation") & (verif.cqa == "aggregates_hmw")].iloc[0]
assert bool(_vviagg["widening_supported"]) and abs(float(both.downstream_added) - float(_vviagg["predicted_nor_bound95"])) < 1e-3
both_net = "stricter" if both.iac_high < both.iac_high_apriori else "wider"
vi_agg_bound, vi_agg_plat = T.num(_vviagg["predicted_nor_bound95"]), T.num(_vviagg["assumed"])
cex_agg_bound = T.num(_vcexagg["predicted_nor_bound95"])
tonly_list = join_and(_crit_phrase(r) for r in _tonly.itertuples())
wonly_list = join_and(_crit_phrase(r) for r in _wonly.itertuples())
both_phrase = _crit_phrase(both)

# --- verification outcomes ---
_vt = verif[verif["met"].notna()]
_vwid = _vt[_vt["met"].astype(bool) & _vt["widening_supported"].astype(bool)]
def _better(r):
    return (r.predicted_nor_bound95 > r.assumed) if r.assumption == "fold_min" else (r.predicted_nor_bound95 < r.assumed)
_bet = _vt.apply(lambda r: _better(r), axis=1).astype(bool)
_vinad = _vt[_vt["met"].astype(bool) & _bet & ~_vt["widening_supported"].astype(bool)]
_vcon = _vt[_vt["met"].astype(bool) & ~_bet]
assert not _vinad["model_adequate"].astype(bool).any()       # bettered, but the model fails adequacy
assert _vwid["model_adequate"].astype(bool).all()
n_verif_inad = len(_vinad)
n_verif_widen, n_verif_conf = len(_vwid), len(_vcon)
assert n_verif_failed == 1 and n_verif_widen > 1 and n_verif_untestable > 1
assert n_verif_widen + n_verif_inad + n_verif_conf == n_verif_met
assert set(verif.loc[verif["met"].isna(), "cqa"]) == {"leached_protein_a"}
assert set(verif.loc[verif["met"].isna(), "step_key"]) == {"cex", "aex"}
_vf = _vt[~_vt["met"].astype(bool)].iloc[0]
assert _vf["step_key"] == "cex" and _vf["cqa"] == "aggregates_hmw"
VSTEP = {"viral_inactivation": "low-pH viral inactivation", "cex": "cation exchange", "aex": "anion exchange"}
def _vname(r):
    kind = "clearance" if r.assumption == "fold_min" else "increase"
    return f"the {CQA_WORD[r.cqa]} {kind} of {VSTEP[r.step_key]}"
vwid_list = join_and(_vname(r) for r in _vwid.itertuples())
vcon_sentence = (f"For {join_and(_vname(r) for r in _vcon.itertuples())}, the predicted worst case confirmed "
                 "the platform worst case, but the prediction bound of a single batch is not better than it, "
                 "so the platform values stand." if n_verif_conf else "")
vinad_list = join_and(_vname(r) for r in _vinad.itertuples()) if n_verif_inad else ""
vinad_sentence = (f"For {vinad_list} the prediction bound of a single batch was also better, but the model does "
                  "not meet the model adequacy criteria, so the platform values stand." if n_verif_inad else "")
vinad_con_text = " ".join(s for s in (vinad_sentence, vcon_sentence) if s)
vtest_steps = join_and(VSTEP[k] for k in dict.fromkeys(_vt["step_key"]))
# the bound is the conservative side of the point prediction
assert all((r.predicted_nor_bound95 <= r.predicted_nor) if r.assumption == "fold_min"
           else (r.predicted_nor_bound95 >= r.predicted_nor) for r in _vt.itertuples())

# --- the bound that may replace a platform worst case (owner, 2026-10-09; PCMP-001 §7.5) ---
# the one-sided prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable NOR combination of the
# downstream step, never a confidence bound of the mean: every platform worst case the criteria rely on
# concerns a quality attribute, and a quality attribute is judged per batch
vb = f"{100 * D.VERIFICATION_BOUND:g}"
assert not any(str(c).startswith("lrv") for c in verif["cqa"])
assert all(D.decision_statistic(r) == "batch" for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "lmw_cesds_pct", "acidic_variants"))

# --- why the low-pH replacements moved, per attribute (PCP-006 factual check, 2026-10-09) ---
# the platform worst cases of the low-pH hold are increases over a 180-min hold (iac.platform sources);
# the A-Mab values are the increases within the hold-time NOR as characterized. The edges of the range
# studied include the platform's hold. Where A-Mab adds at least the platform value there, the replacement
# reflects the shorter hold only; where it adds less even there, A-Mab also adds less over the same hold.
_hold = CFG.unit_op("viral_inactivation").param("hold_time")
_plat_hold = {re.search(r"(\d+) min", p["source"]).group(1) for p in _plat["viral_inactivation"].values()}
assert len(_plat_hold) == 1
plat_hold = _plat_hold.pop()
vi_hold_hi = g(_hold.nor_characterized[1])
assert float(plat_hold) > float(_hold.nor_characterized[1])      # the A-Mab hold is the shorter
assert float(_hold.nor[1]) <= float(_hold.nor_characterized[1])  # routine manufacture holds no longer
assert float(_hold.prange[1]) >= float(plat_hold)                # the edges include the platform's hold
_vwid_vi = _vwid[_vwid["step_key"] == "viral_inactivation"]
assert len(_vwid_vi) > 0 and (_vwid_vi["assumption"] == "add_max").all()
assert all(T.ATTR_NAME[c].endswith("(%)") for c in _vwid_vi["cqa"])   # "percentage points"
_vi_hold_only = [r for r in _vwid_vi.itertuples() if r.observed_edge >= r.assumed]
_vi_also_less = [r for r in _vwid_vi.itertuples() if r.observed_edge < r.assumed]
_why = ([f"For {CQA_WORD[r.cqa]}, the largest increase measured at the edges of the range studied, which "
         f"include a hold of {plat_hold} min, is {T.num(r.observed_edge)} percentage points, above the platform "
         f"value of {T.num(r.assumed)}. Its replacement therefore reflects the shorter hold of A-Mab, not a more "
         f"stable product." for r in _vi_hold_only]
        + [f"For {CQA_WORD[r.cqa]}, the largest increase measured at the edges of the range studied is "
           f"{T.num(r.observed_edge)} percentage points, below the platform value of {T.num(r.assumed)} even over a "
           f"hold of {plat_hold} min. A-Mab therefore adds less than the platform products over the same hold, and "
           f"its shorter hold lowers the increase further." for r in _vi_also_less])
vi_rep_text = (f"The platform worst cases of the low-pH hold are increases over a hold of {plat_hold} min. The "
               f"A-Mab {'bounds are the increases' if len(_vwid_vi) > 1 else 'bound is the increase'} within the "
               f"hold-time NOR as characterized, which ends at {vi_hold_hi} min. " + " ".join(_why) +
               f" The criteria calculated with {'these bounds' if len(_vwid_vi) > 1 else 'this bound'} are still "
               "right, because routine manufacture never holds longer than the NOR.")

    + [f"For {CQA_WORD[r.cqa]} A-Mab adds less than the platform value even over a hold of {plat_hold} min."
       for r in _vi_also_less])
# the criteria upstream of the low-pH hold that its replacements widened (the bioreactor harvest)
_wvi = _wide[(_wide["step_key"].map(steps.index) < steps.index("viral_inactivation"))
             & _wide["cqa"].isin(set(_vwid_vi["cqa"]))]
assert len(_wvi) > 0
_vi_order = list(_vwid_vi["cqa"])
wvi_phrase = join_and(f"the criteria for {join_and(CQA_WORD[c] for c in sorted(grp['cqa'], key=_vi_order.index))} "
                      f"in the {POOL[k]}" for k, grp in _wvi.groupby("step_key", sort=False))

_vcexhcp = verif[(verif.step_key == "cex") & (verif.cqa == "hcp")].iloc[0]
_vaexhcp = verif[(verif.step_key == "aex") & (verif.cqa == "hcp")].iloc[0]
# Protein A and CEX pool host cell protein: which downstream bound replaced the platform value
assert bool(_vcexhcp["met"]) and bool(_vaexhcp["met"])           # neither tightens a host cell protein criterion
assert (_vcexhcp["assumption"], _vaexhcp["assumption"]) == ("fold_min", "fold_min")
_hcp_rep = [k for k, v in (("cex", _vcexhcp), ("aex", _vaexhcp)) if bool(v["widening_supported"])]
_hcp_inad = [k for k, v in (("cex", _vcexhcp), ("aex", _vaexhcp)) if _better(v) and not bool(v["widening_supported"])]
_hcp_con = [k for k, v in (("cex", _vcexhcp), ("aex", _vaexhcp)) if not _better(v)]
assert len(_hcp_rep) > 0 and bool(r_pa_hcp["widened"])
assert bool(r_cex_hcp["widened"]) == ("aex" in _hcp_rep)
# no cross-reference inside a computed string: Quarto does not resolve one there, and citeproc
# printed "(sec?)-acc-model" (PCP-006 author, 2026-10-09); the references follow in the text
_HN = {"cex": "cation exchange", "aex": "anion exchange"}
_hv = {"cex": _vcexhcp, "aex": _vaexhcp}

_dz = _mp[_mp["kind"].isin(["screening", "rsm", "superseded"]) & _mp["lmw_in_scope"].astype(bool)]

# Parameter.nor / .setpoint are in force; .nor_characterized / .setpoint_characterized are the values the
# studies were planned against. A NOR is "narrowed" when the new one lies inside the old and is shorter,
# "moved" when it keeps its width; no other change is described here.
_nchg = {}                          # step -> list of (kind, parameter name, set-point moved)
for _k in steps:
    for _pp in CFG.unit_op(_k).parameters:
        _new, _old = [float(x) for x in _pp.nor], [float(x) for x in _pp.nor_characterized]
        _spm = float(_pp.setpoint) != float(_pp.setpoint_characterized)
        if _new == _old:
            assert not _spm         # a set-point moved inside an unchanged NOR is not described here
            continue
        if _old[0] <= _new[0] and _new[1] <= _old[1] and (_new[1] - _new[0]) < (_old[1] - _old[0]):
            _kind = "narrowed"
        else:
            assert abs((_new[1] - _new[0]) - (_old[1] - _old[0])) < 1e-9

assert len(_nchg) >= 1

             "viral_inactivation": "low-pH viral inactivation", "cex": "cation exchange", "aex": "anion exchange",
             "virus_filtration": "virus filtration", "ufdf": "UF/DF"}
def _chg_clause(k):
    ch = _nchg[k]
    mv = [n for kind, n, _ in ch if kind == "moved"]
    nr = [n for kind, n, _ in ch if kind == "narrowed"]
    mv_sp = [n for kind, n, s in ch if kind == "moved" and s]

    assert set(mv_sp) == set(mv)    # a moved NOR carries its set-point with it
    parts = []
    if mv:
        parts.append(f"moved the NOR and the set-point of {join_and(mv)}")
    if nr:
        parts.append(f"narrowed the {'NORs' if len(nr) > 1 else 'NOR'} of {join_and(nr)}"
                     + (f", with a new set-point for {join_and(nr_sp)}" if nr_sp else ""))
    return f"The {REPORT_OF[k]} report PCR-{CFG.unit_op(k).step:03d} " + ", and ".join(parts) + "."
nar_text = " ".join(_chg_clause(k) for k in _nchg)
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan governs the Stage 1 process characterization of the A-Mab drug substance process. It sits under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001, which moves the process from the development site in `{python} dev_site`, to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} com_site`. The characterization studies provide the evidence for the operating ranges and the control strategy that are transferred.

The plan covers the `{python} n_steps` steps of the drug substance train listed in @tbl-train, from the `{python} first_title.lower()` (Step `{python} first_step`) to `{python} last_title.lower()` (Step `{python} last_step`). The seed expansion steps and the drug product process are outside its scope.

```{python}
#| output: asis
#| label: tbl-train
#| tbl-cap: "The drug substance process train and the principal role of each step."
show(steps_tab)
```

This plan sets out the critical quality attribute (CQA) framework (@sec-cqa), the risk basis (@sec-risk), the common approach to scale-down models (@sec-sdm) and to statistics (@sec-stats), and the framework of acceptance criteria (@sec-acceptance) for the whole train. Each Process Characterization Plan (PCP-003 to PCP-010) applies this framework to one step. It adds what is specific to that step, such as the scale-down model, the factors and their ranges, and the sampling plan. Where a step plan departs from this plan, it should state the departure and the reason for it.

The documents of the package build on each other in sequence. The risk assessment RA-001 sets the scope of each study. The Process Characterization Plan of the step (PCP-00N) plans the study, and the paired Process Characterization Report (PCR-00N) reports it. The Process Characterization Master Report PCMR-001 then consolidates the reports into the control strategy for the whole process. The QA investigation INV-001 reviewed PCMR-001 Version 1.0, and its findings led back to this revision and to the reissue of the other documents. @tbl-docs lists the package.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(docs_tab, "Documents of the A-Mab characterization package.", "tbl-docs", merge=["Subject"],
        align=["P{8.0cm}", "l", "P{5.4cm}"]).show()
```

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version `{python} rev1_ver` of this plan was approved on `{python} rev1_eff`, `{python} 'before' if plan_before_studies else 'after'` the first characterization study started on `{python} first_start`. Version `{python} ver` replaces it and is issued under `{python} inv_id`. QA opened the investigation on `{python} inv_open` after its review of PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness, and closed it on `{python} inv_close` with the classification `{python} inv_class`. INV-001 found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range (PAR) analysis were not in any approved protocol and had been set after the data were seen (INV-001 finding 1). Of the `{python} n_rev1` Version 1.0 step criteria, the `{python} n_margin` `{python} margin_class` criteria had been carried back from the drug substance limit through the nominal clearance of this campaign and then divided by a margin that differed by step (INV-001 finding 2). Version 1.0 of this plan defined no criteria for step outputs.

This revision makes the following changes.

1. It defines intermediate acceptance criteria (IACs) for the step outputs on which a drug substance criterion depends (@sec-iac). The rule that derives them uses no data from the studies it judges. They replace the Version 1.0 step criteria described above (INV-001 findings 1 and 2). They also replace the bioreactor limits for the glycans and acidic variants, which were computed from the capability data they were then used to judge (INV-001 finding 3).
2. It defines how each report verifies the platform worst cases that the criteria rely on, and when that verification may change a criterion (@sec-verification). Verification tightens a criterion where a step does worse within its NOR than the platform worst case. It widens a criterion only where the one-sided `{python} vb` % prediction bound of a single batch, at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the step, is better than the platform value and the model behind it is adequate. In both directions this bound replaces the platform value, and neither the point prediction nor a confidence bound of the mean ever does. A report whose verification changes a criterion argues the change by its risk.
3. It qualifies each scale-down model by its offset from manufacturing scale, not by a test of equivalence, and states every judgement against a criterion at manufacturing scale (@sec-acc-sdm).
4. It sets non-reduced CE-SDS (nrCE-SDS) as the method for fragments at every step, following the decision of `{python} amd_date` to change the fragment method to nrCE-SDS (`{python} amd_id`, @sec-fragments). This answers INV-001 finding 6, that size exclusion chromatography (SEC) reads fragments high in samples that still carry host cell protein.
5. It assesses capability for acidic variants against both ends of the criterion (@sec-capability). Version 1.0 assessed it against the upper end only (INV-001 finding 4).
6. It judges viral clearance at the worst case within the NOR (@sec-par). That is the mean predicted log reduction with the other parameters at their least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. Viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions, so the claim must hold there. Quality attributes are judged on a single batch. Version 1.0 judged every response on a single batch.
7. It records the execution window of every study and the calibration status of the equipment each study used (@sec-sdm and @sec-schedule). The Version 1.0 records gave no execution dates, so the equipment tables appeared to cite expired calibrations (INV-001 finding 5). The Version 1.0 title blocks of the plans also carried `{python} pkg_rev1`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved, in place of the date each plan was approved. The revision history of this plan now gives the approval date.
8. It states campaign thresholds for the significance of model terms (@sec-stats), for model adequacy (@sec-acc-model) and for capability (@sec-acc-capability). Version 1.0 left all three to the individual study.

In Version 1.0 the cation exchange pool was judged against an aggregate limit of `{python} r1_cex_agg_hi` % HMW. That limit was the drug substance criterion of `{python} ds_agg` % divided by a margin of `{python} r1_cex_agg_margin`. The derivation in this plan credits no step after cation exchange with aggregate removal. The cation exchange pool therefore carries the drug substance criterion itself, `{python} cex_agg_iac` % (@tbl-iac). The Version 1.0 limit was never an approved criterion, because it was applied at analysis and appeared in no approved plan, so the wider criterion now in force replaces no approved value. What moved at each step as a result is stated in the "Changes in this revision" section of its PCR-00N, from its own data.

# Stage 1 characterization strategy {#sec-strategy}

Process validation follows a lifecycle, and its first stage is process design [@fda2011]. In Stage 1 the commercial process is defined from the knowledge gained in development, and the studies that support it are documented. This campaign follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8 and ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11]. Prior knowledge and risk assessment identify which parameters may affect which attributes. Characterization studies then measure those effects and bound them. The result is a set of normal operating ranges (NORs), PARs and parameter classes, from which the control strategy is built [@amab2009].

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 antibody developed on the Novacyte platform. The downstream train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, virus filtration and UF/DF was used for three earlier antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. Their history establishes the mechanism of each step and the range of performance to expect from it. Characterization of A-Mab therefore confirms and bounds known behaviour. The same history supplies the worst case of each downstream step, on which the intermediate acceptance criteria are built (@sec-iac).

Criticality is treated as a continuum, as described in ICH Q8(R2) [@ichq8]. RA-001 ranks each parameter and assigns it to multivariate study, to univariate study or to no new study (@sec-risk). Parameters assigned to multivariate study are characterized by designed experiments in a scale-down model. The qualification runs of the model come before the designs, and the decision whether the model is qualified is made at analysis (@sec-sdm). Such designs are planned for `{python} n_doe` steps, from the production bioreactor to virus filtration. The `{python} nodoe_names` steps are characterized by univariate and qualitative studies only, because RA-001 assigned none of their parameters to multivariate study.

Against the NOR in force (@tbl-parameters-by-step), the characterized range is wider than the NOR at both ends for `{python} n_wide_both` of the `{python} n_par` parameters. For `{python} n_one_end` parameters (`{python} one_end_names`) the low end of the characterized range equals the low end of the NOR, and only the high end extends beyond it. For `{python} equal_names` the NOR equals the characterized range. Where the range is wider, it shows how the process behaves near and beyond the edges of routine operation. It also gives the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed. A PAR is claimed only where the data support it, and never beyond the range studied.

Viral safety rests on modular and orthogonal clearance across low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration [@ichq5a]. Each of these steps is studied in its own spiking model, and each step plan claims only the log reduction of its own step. The cumulative claim is consolidated in PCMR-001.

The outputs of Stage 1 feed process performance qualification at the receiving site. PTP-001 plans `{python} n_ppq` PPQ batches. The ranges and classes that this campaign supports are the ones those batches will be run against.

# Critical quality attribute framework {#sec-cqa}

The CQAs and their drug substance acceptance criteria are taken from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. Several of the criteria were set there from clinical experience with X-Mab, the closest platform antibody. They are held in the drug substance CQA register, and @tbl-cqa lists all `{python} n_cqa` attributes. Criticality was assigned with Tool #1 of the case study, as the product of impact and uncertainty. The levels run from very low (VL) to very high (VH), and the Tool #1 score stands beside each level. For every attribute except viral clearance, a higher score gives an equal or higher level. The two viral clearance attributes were assigned very high criticality by rule, because a viral contamination would directly harm the patient, whatever the uncertainty term of the score gives.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cqa_tab2, "Drug substance CQA register, with acceptance criteria, criticality and the step at which each attribute is formed or set.",
        "tbl-cqa", merge=["Category"], header={"Tool #1": "Tool #1\nscore", "Formed or set at": "Formed or\nset at"},
        align=["P{2.4cm}", "P{3.8cm}", "P{3.4cm}", "l", "r", "P{2.8cm}"]).show()
```

The last column of @tbl-cqa names the step at which each attribute is formed or set. Most attributes are formed in the production bioreactor. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose are formed there, and no downstream step changes them. Protein A binds the Fc region at the interface of the CH2 and CH3 domains, so it captures every glycan variant alike. The two ion exchange steps do not separate glycan variants under platform conditions [@amab2009]. Leached Protein A enters the process at capture. Fragments are formed in culture and during the harvest hold, by proteases released from lysed cells that clip the antibody. The register therefore assigns them to harvest. No criterion for fragments is set at harvest, and they are judged at the downstream steps (@tbl-iac). They are not an attribute of the production bioreactor designs (@tbl-methods-by-study).

The two viral clearance attributes are cumulative. The register assigns each to one step, but each requirement is met by the sum of the claims of several steps (@sec-viral).

The attributes of very low criticality (`{python} vl_names`) remain in the register, and their criteria apply.

The output of a step that removes an impurity, or that adds to a variant, is judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion derived from the drug substance criterion (@sec-iac).

# Risk-based prioritization {#sec-risk}

RA-001 assessed every process parameter of the train before characterization began. Each parameter was ranked on its potential impact on the CQAs and on process performance, and on its potential to interact with other parameters. Parameters ranked high, or with a likely interaction, were assigned to multivariate study. Parameters ranked lower, whose range could be supported one factor at a time, were assigned to univariate study. RA-001 gives the scores and the rationale for each assignment, and they are not repeated here.

@tbl-scope shows the result across the train. Of the `{python} n_par` parameters, `{python} n_mv` are studied in multivariate designs and `{python} n_uv` one factor at a time. All `{python} n_nodoe_par` parameters of `{python} nodoe_names` are studied univariately.

```{python}
                "Multivariate": "In multivariate\ndesigns", "Univariate": "One factor\nat a time"},
        align=["r", "P{4.4cm}", "r", "r", "r", "l"]).show()
```

@tbl-parameters-by-step lists every parameter with its set-point, NOR and characterized range. The set-point and the NOR shown are those in force. Some of them were changed at Version 2.0 by the report of their step, after the studies. `{python} nar_text` The table footnotes each change with the value the studies were planned against. The class column gives the classification assigned in each PCR-00N under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001, by the rules in @sec-classification.

The range of a parameter studied univariately is supported by its own data, and its class is decided by the same rules as for a parameter studied in a design.

# Scale-down model strategy {#sec-sdm}

Every characterization study is run in a scale-down model. The model is designed on the scaling principles of its unit operation. Parameters that do not depend on scale are held at their commercial values. Parameters that depend on scale are set so that the model matches the performance of the manufacturing scale. The qualification runs of the model are made under the scale-down model procedure SOP-1001 before the first characterization run of the step, and the offset of each output from manufacturing scale is estimated from them. The decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made later, at analysis. That decision needs the response-surface model of the step, because it compares the conclusion over the NOR with the offset at either end of its confidence interval (@sec-acc-sdm).

For the chromatography steps the model keeps the bed height and the residence time of the manufacturing column. Load, wash and elution volumes are normalized to column volumes, and column efficiency is checked by plate count and peak asymmetry. For the production bioreactor the model is a stirred tank with equivalent mixing, aeration and process control. In each study, the parameters not under study are held at their commercial set-points. The designs vary `{python} bio_mv`, and univariate studies vary `{python} bio_uv`. Agitation and gas flow are set to match the oxygen transfer and carbon dioxide stripping of the commercial vessel. For virus filtration the model uses the same filter type as manufacturing, and load is scaled by membrane area. For UF/DF, membrane loading and cross flow are scaled by membrane area.

Qualification compares the scale-down model, run at set-point, with manufacturing-scale batches. The outputs compared are those of `{python} sq_phrase`. A scale-down model need not reproduce the manufacturing mean. The difference between the two scales must instead be known precisely enough that no conclusion depends on its exact size. The rule is in @sec-acc-sdm, and each PCP-00N applies it to its own outputs. A model qualified for one output is not by that fact qualified for another. Where the qualification runs do not compare an output at both scales, the PCP-00N should say so and should state how that output is characterized instead. Where the model is not qualified for an output at analysis, the PCR-00N should say so and should state the consequence.

Viral clearance is studied in a spiking model of each claimed step, because virus cannot be introduced at manufacturing scale. The spiking model follows the same scaling principles as the characterization model of the step [@ichq5a].

The campaign used `{python} n_eq` instrumented scale-down systems under calibration and change control. They are `{python} eq_names`. @tbl-equipment lists each with the studies that used it. `{python} "Every" if eq_all_ok else "Not every"` study window closed before the next calibration due date of the equipment it used. Every study that the Version 1.0 reports analysed closed before those reports were approved on `{python} pkg_rev1`. The last of them ended on `{python} pre_last_end`. One supplementary qualification study of the Protein A scale-down model, `{python} post_ids` (`{python} post_window`), ran afterwards, while `{python} inv_id` was open. Its runs were made to narrow the confidence interval of the offset for host cell protein in the Protein A pool (@sec-acc-sdm). They are work that the Protein A plan `{python} pd_plan` did not foresee, and the Protein A report `{python} pd_report` records them as discrepancy `{python} pd_id` from that plan.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.calibration_windows(label="tbl-equipment").show()
```

Intermediate pools are held between steps. During a hold, aggregate can form, asparagine residues can deamidate and raise the acidic variants, and proteases in the clarified harvest can clip the antibody into fragments. Each of these raises its attribute with time. Version 1.0 of the plans did not study a hold. During the Version 2.0 re-analysis, hold studies were made, from `{python} hold_from` to `{python} hold_to`, on the clarified harvest, the Protein A eluate (at elution pH) and the neutralized viral inactivation pool. Each report records its hold study as a discrepancy from its plan, and no plan describes one. A held pool is judged against the intermediate acceptance criteria that it must meet when it enters the next step (@sec-iac).

Each response is measured by a validated method under its own SOP. @tbl-sops lists every controlled procedure and method validation cited in the package. The SOP and AMV numbers are placeholders.


# Common statistical approach {#sec-stats}

## Designs

Each step with a multivariate scope is studied in two stages, under the design of experiments procedure SOP-1002. A screening design comes first. It is a two-level factorial design, full or fractional as the number of factors requires, with replicated centre points. A response-surface design follows. It is a central composite design over the factors that each step plan carries forward from the screening. It also has replicated centre points. @tbl-designs gives the structure of each design. Every design has at least `{python} min_cp` centre points. The centre points estimate pure error and allow a test for curvature and for lack of fit.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.CTable(header=[[T.C("Step", rs=2), T.C("Unit operation", rs=2), T.C("Screening", cs=3), T.C("Response surface", cs=2), T.C("Responses", rs=2)],
                 ["Factors", "Runs", "Model terms", "Factors", "Runs"]],
         body=[[str(v) for v in r] for r in design_tab.itertuples(index=False)],
         caption="Designed experiments per step. Runs are given with the number of centre points in brackets.",
         label="tbl-designs", align=["r", "P{2.8cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "P{5.6cm}"]).show()
```

Runs are executed in random order within each design. Where a run is lost or invalidated, the PCR-00N should report it and state whether the design was repaired or re-executed.

## Models, and what each model is for

The screening data are fitted with a model of main effects and two-factor interactions in coded units. The response-surface data are fitted with a full quadratic model. Effects are reported as the change in the response over the coded range of the factor, and a model term is significant when its p-value is below α = `{python} effect_alpha`. This is the conventional level. Its consequence is that about one term in twenty with no real effect is called significant by chance. An attribute is called affected by a parameter when a term that contains the parameter is significant at that level.

The screening model identifies effects. Its centre points detect curvature but cannot attribute it to a factor, and the model still interpolates linearly between the corners of the design. In the `{python} sat_names` screening designs the interaction model also leaves only `{python} sat_lof` degree of freedom for lack of fit (@tbl-designs), so its fit statistics overstate how well it fits. The response-surface model is the predictive model. Every prediction, every PAR and every design space in the package comes from it. No report should claim prediction from a screening model.

A response-surface model predicts the mean response over the range studied. At the edge of an acceptable region defined on mean predictions, a single batch meets its criterion about half the time if variability is symmetrical. For this reason a quality attribute is judged on a single batch, not on the mean prediction, in three analyses. The NOR-propagated proven acceptable range (@sec-par) is computed by Monte Carlo, and its interval includes the model residual, the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients and the variation of the other parameters within their NOR. The judgement of an output over the NOR in the scale-down qualification (@sec-acc-sdm) uses the exact 95 % prediction interval of a single run at each combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. The verification of the platform worst cases (@sec-verification) uses the one-sided `{python} vb` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable of these combinations.

## Model adequacy

Each fitted model is reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R², the model F-test, and the lack-of-fit test against pure error from the centre points. Residuals are inspected against predicted values and on a normal probability plot. A model is used for prediction only if it meets the adequacy criteria in @sec-acc-model.

## Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

A PAR is computed for each CQA that has a criterion at the step and for each factor of the response-surface model.

1. The set-point analysis is a univariate proven acceptable range with the other parameters at their set-points. It scans the factor across its characterized range. The PAR is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the mean prediction meets the criterion.
2. The NOR-propagated analysis is the same range with the other parameters varying within their NORs. It scans the factor across `{python} par_grid` grid points. The PAR is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the predicted result meets the criterion.

What the NOR-propagated analysis compares with the criterion depends on the kind of attribute.

- For a quality attribute it compares the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch, because a single batch is what must meet the criterion. At each grid point the analysis draws `{python} f"{par_mc:,}"` operating points for the other factors. Each factor is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of one sixth of the width of its NOR, and clipped to the characterized range. This assumes that the NOR spans ±3 standard deviations of the routine variation of the parameter. The interval includes the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients. It runs from the 2.5th to the 97.5th percentile of the simulated batches. For an upper limit the 97.5th percentile must not exceed the limit, for a lower limit the 2.5th percentile must not fall below it, and for a two-sided criterion both apply.
- For viral clearance it compares the worst case within the NOR. At each grid point the other factors are set to every combination of their NOR low, set-point and NOR high. The lowest mean predicted log reduction among these combinations must meet the claim of the step. Viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions, so a claim that held only on average over the NOR would not support a validated log reduction.

The NOR-propagated PAR is the one that supports a claim. It is in general narrower than the set-point PAR, because the range must hold while the rest of the operating point moves within its NOR.

## Capability, and the integrated model {#sec-capability}

Capability at commercial scale is estimated from an integrated model of the train. The model runs `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` simulated batches through every step in sequence. Each process parameter of each batch is drawn from the same normal distribution as in the NOR-propagated analysis of a quality attribute (@sec-par). The drug substance attributes of each batch are recorded.

Capability is reported as Cpk against the drug substance criterion. For a criterion with one limit, Cpk is computed against that limit. For a two-sided criterion it is the lower of the two one-sided indices. Acidic variants have a two-sided criterion (`{python} acid_lo` to `{python} acid_hi` %), and their capability is assessed against both ends. The criteria for capability are in @sec-acc-capability.

The same simulation gives the probability of an out-of-specification drug substance for each attribute. Two figures are reported, because a few thousand simulated batches cannot resolve a rare event. These are the count of simulated batches outside the criterion, and the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard deviation, one- or two-sided as the criterion is. The intermediate acceptance criteria judge each step separately, and the integrated model shows whether the steps together deliver the drug substance.

# Acceptance criteria framework {#sec-acceptance}

Each PCP-00N applies the criteria below to its own step. They define when a scale-down model is qualified, a model adequate, a step output acceptable, a range proven and a parameter classified. Where a value depends on the step, this plan defines the form of the criterion and the step plan sets its value. In Version 1.0 each step plan was approved before its studies ran. The a priori derivation of the Version 2.0 criteria came after the studies, and for that reason it uses platform data and the drug substance criteria only (@sec-iac). Verification then replaced some platform values with A-Mab prediction bounds of a single batch, and `{python} n_moved` of the `{python} n_iac` criteria in force include such a bound (@sec-verification).

## Scale-down model qualification {#sec-acc-sdm}

A scale-down model is qualified for each output separately. It is qualified by the offset between the scales, not by a test of equivalence. A model may differ in mean from manufacturing scale, provided the difference is known precisely enough. The rule has four parts.

1. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches. It is reported with its two-sided `{python} offset_ci` % confidence interval. Each end of that interval is a one-sided `{python} offset_side` % confidence bound, which is the level used to compare two means at 5 % on each side.
2. Where the qualification compared an output at both scales, every judgement of a scale-down result for that output against a criterion first subtracts its offset. Ranges and conclusions are therefore stated at manufacturing scale.
3. The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its confidence interval. The conclusion is whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the response-surface factors.
4. An output with no criterion at the step, such as step yield, has its offset recorded only. No conclusion depends on it.

Where the cause of an offset is known, the report states it. A model whose conclusion for an output changes between the two ends of the offset interval is not used for that output. The qualification studies do not compare fragments or viral clearance at both scales. Their offset is unknown, not zero. These outputs are judged as the model predicts them because the qualification did not compare them, and their representativeness rests on what each step plan states, which is the mechanism of the step for fragments and the spiking model for viral clearance.

Each PCP-00N names the outputs, the number of runs at each scale and the manufacturing-scale data set. The scale-down runs at set-point are made, and the offset of each output is estimated, before the first characterization run of the step. The decision whether the model is qualified for an output needs the response-surface model of the step, because the conclusion over the NOR comes from that model. That decision is therefore made at analysis. Each PCR-00N tabulates the offsets of its step, and PCMR-001 summarises them for the whole train.

## Model adequacy {#sec-acc-model}

A response-surface model is adequate for prediction when the following hold.

1. The model F-test is significant at the level set for model terms, α = `{python} effect_alpha` (@sec-stats).
2. Lack of fit against pure error is not significant at α = `{python} lof_alpha`.
3. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} max_gap`. This is a limit on overfitting, because a model that fits its own runs much better than it predicts left-out runs has more terms than the data support.
4. The residuals show no pattern against predicted values or run order, and no single run dominates the fit.

A model that fails the lack-of-fit test or the limit on overfitting is either refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, or it is not used to set a range.

Where no adequate model results, the PCR-00N should report the response descriptively, against the criterion, over the runs of the design.

## Intermediate acceptance criteria {#sec-iac}

A drug substance criterion does not say what the output of an upstream step must meet. Protein A, for example, leaves host cell protein in its pool that cation exchange and anion exchange will remove. The Protein A pool is expected to carry far more host cell protein than the drug substance limit of `{python} ds_hcp` ng/mg, so that limit cannot judge it. Each step output is therefore judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion.

The rule is the following. Each drug substance criterion is carried backward through the train, step by step, using the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform. For a step that removes an attribute, the worst case is the lowest clearance fold observed for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. For a step that adds to an attribute, it is the largest increase observed. No margin is applied. An attribute that no downstream step changes keeps its drug substance criterion. This is the case for afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose.

For host cell protein the rule gives the Protein A pool an a priori criterion of `{python} pa_hcp_apriori` ng/mg. The drug substance limit of `{python} ds_hcp` ng/mg is carried back through the platform worst case of anion exchange (`{python} plat_aex_hcp`-fold) and then of cation exchange (`{python} plat_cex_hcp`-fold). The cation exchange pool is judged against the limit carried back through anion exchange alone, `{python} cex_hcp_apriori` ng/mg a priori. For A-Mab, the one-sided `{python} vb` % prediction bounds of a single batch for the host cell protein clearance were `{python} cex_hcp_bound`-fold for cation exchange and `{python} aex_hcp_bound`-fold for anion exchange (@sec-verification). `{python} hcp_cmp_text` (@sec-acc-model). The Protein A pool criterion is therefore `{python} pa_hcp_iac` ng/mg, and the cation exchange pool criterion `{python} cex_hcp_verb` `{python} cex_hcp_iac` ng/mg.

@tbl-iac gives all `{python} n_iac` criteria across `{python} n_iac_steps` steps, with the downstream worst case each one is derived from, platform or verified. The downstream worst case shown is the cumulative fold or increase of all steps after the step output. In a tightened or a widened row it includes a verified A-Mab value, the prediction bound of a single batch that replaced a platform worst case (@sec-verification). The footnotes of the table mark these rows. The source of each platform value is recorded in the configuration of the process model and in the verification table of each report.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation().show()
```

The rule above credits each downstream step only with the clearance or increase in its platform history and assumes no other change in its operation. Note `{python} iac_note_ds` of @tbl-iac marks the rows where no downstream step is credited, so the drug substance criterion applies. A hold between steps can still raise aggregate and acidic variants (@sec-sdm). A held pool must therefore still meet the criteria of this section when it enters the next step. The reports judge the hold studies made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis against them.

Residual DNA has a drug substance criterion but no intermediate acceptance criterion. The Protein A designs measure DNA in the load and the pool, but the platform history used here gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A, so no criterion can be carried back. Residual DNA is therefore judged on the drug substance only, and its capability is assessed in the integrated model (@sec-capability).

Of the `{python} n_iac` criteria in @tbl-iac, `{python} n_apriori` are in force at their a priori value and verification changed `{python} n_moved`. The tightened criteria are the aggregate criteria upstream of cation exchange, because the cation exchange model gave a lower aggregate clearance than the platform worst case. One of them, `{python} both_phrase`, was also widened, because the low-pH viral inactivation model gave a smaller aggregate increase (`{python} vi_agg_bound` % at the prediction bound of a single batch, against `{python} vi_agg_plat` % on the platform). The result is a `{python} both_net` criterion than the a priori one. The other tightened criterion is `{python} tonly_list`. The criteria only widened are `{python} wonly_list`. The widening of `{python} wvi_phrase` comes from low-pH viral inactivation. There the A-Mab hold is at most `{python} vi_hold_hi` min within its NOR as characterized, and the platform worst cases are increases over a hold of `{python} plat_hold` min. `{python} vi_why_short` Every report that relies on a changed criterion argues the change by its risk (@sec-verification).

Applying these criteria to studies already executed is acceptable because the a priori derivation uses no data from the studies it judges. The drug substance criteria come from the CQA register. The worst cases come from the platform history of X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. A-Mab data enter a criterion only when verification replaces a platform worst case with the one-sided `{python} vb` % prediction bound of a single batch for the same step (@sec-verification).

## Viral clearance claims {#sec-viral}

Each step that clears virus is held to its platform claim. The claim is the log reduction that the step has delivered for that virus on the platform, with X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. The sum of the claims is then checked against the cumulative requirement of the drug substance. @tbl-viral shows that check for each model virus. Each step is then judged against its own claim at the worst case within its NOR, as @sec-par defines it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(vc_tab, "Platform claims per step (log10) and their sum against the cumulative requirement of the drug substance.", "tbl-viral",
        header={"Low-pH viral inactivation": "Low-pH viral\ninactivation", "Anion exchange": "Anion\nexchange",
                "Virus filtration": "Virus\nfiltration", "Sum of claims": "Sum of\nclaims", "Cumulative requirement": "Cumulative\nrequirement"},
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"]).show()
```

The claims for XMuLV sum to `{python} f"{xm.claimed_sum:.2f}"` log10 against a requirement of `{python} g(xm.required)`. For MVM they sum to `{python} f"{mv.claimed_sum:.2f}"` against `{python} g(mv.required)`. `{python} "Both requirements are met" if vc_all_met else "Not every requirement is met"` by the claims alone, with little room above them. A step that falls short of its claim therefore cannot be made up by the surplus of another step. Low-pH viral inactivation makes no claim for MVM, because a parvovirus has no lipid envelope for low pH to disrupt.

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-verification}

Each intermediate acceptance criterion assumes that every downstream step performs at least as well as its platform worst case. That is, the step clears at least the lowest fold, or adds no more than the largest increase, seen for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. Each report checks the platform worst cases of its own step. The check evaluates the response-surface model of the step at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of its factors. These are the NOR and the set-point as characterized, the values the studies were planned against, so a later change of a NOR or a set-point by a report does not move a criterion. The model gives the worst clearance fold, or the largest increase, that it predicts over these combinations. The model also gives the one-sided `{python} vb` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination, on its unfavourable side. An assumption is confirmed when the predicted worst case is no worse than the platform worst case. The values observed at the edges of the characterized range are reported beside it for information.

The bound is a prediction bound of a single batch, never a confidence bound of the mean. Each platform worst case that the criteria rely on concerns a quality attribute, and a quality attribute is judged on a single batch (@sec-stats). The platform worst case that the bound may replace was itself the result of a single run. A confidence bound of the mean describes the average batch, and a single batch can fall beyond it. A bound from a tolerance interval would be statistically purer, because it covers a stated proportion of all batches with a stated confidence. Such a bound would also be wider, and too conservative to set against a platform worst case that was one run. The prediction bound of a single batch is therefore used.

Verification may change a criterion in either direction, by the following rule.

1. Where the A-Mab worst case predicted within the NOR is worse than the platform worst case, the prediction bound of a single batch replaces the platform value. Every criterion upstream of that step is recalculated with it and becomes stricter.
2. Where the prediction bound of a single batch is better than the platform value, and the response-surface model behind it meets the adequacy criteria of @sec-acc-model, the bound replaces the platform value. Every criterion upstream of that step is recalculated with it and becomes wider.
3. Otherwise the platform value stands.

In both directions the bound, on its unfavourable side, replaces the platform value, and the point prediction never does.

Every change of a criterion is argued by its risk. A report whose verification tightens or widens a criterion gives that argument in four parts.

1. The report states who bears the risk of the change, the patient or the producer.
2. The report states whether an excursion of the step output beyond the changed criterion would be detected, and where, by an in-process test or by a release test.
3. The report states what the downstream steps must then clear.
4. The report gives the probability of an out-of-specification drug substance from the integrated model (@sec-capability).

A report that relies on a widened criterion also gives the bound, the runs behind it, and the reason why the performance of the downstream step for A-Mab is known well enough to replace the platform value. The rule was written into this plan before any Version 2.0 step report used it. This reissue of the plan also records what the rule gave, in @sec-iac and below.

The criteria assume `{python} n_verif` platform worst cases. Of these, `{python} n_verif_testable` are responses of the response-surface designs of `{python} vtest_steps`, and they can be checked. The other `{python} n_verif_untestable` are the leached Protein A clearance of cation exchange and of anion exchange. Leached Protein A is not a response of those designs, so the platform values stand. The prediction bound of a single batch was better than the platform worst case for `{python} vwid_list`, and these bounds replaced the platform values. `{python} vi_rep_text`

`{python} vinad_con_text` Verification found that the aggregate clearance of cation exchange within its NOR is lower than the platform worst case. That tightened the aggregate criteria upstream of cation exchange (@sec-iac). The cation exchange report PCR-007 gives the values and their analysis.

## Proven acceptable ranges

A range of a parameter is proven acceptable for an attribute when the NOR-propagated analysis (@sec-par) meets the criterion of that attribute across it. The criterion is the IAC where @tbl-iac defines one, and the drug substance criterion otherwise. A parameter that affects several attributes has a PAR for each, and the range carried into the control strategy is their intersection. Where the output does not meet its criterion even at the set-point, the PCR-00N reports that no PAR exists for the attribute and states the consequence for the NOR.

A PAR that reaches the edge of the characterized range is reported as reaching it, and no claim is made beyond it.

## Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

Parameters are classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001 by the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

1. A critical process parameter (CPP) has an effect on a CQA that is significant and practically relevant within the characterized range, and a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation.
2. A well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) has the same kind of effect on a CQA but a low risk of falling outside its acceptable range, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR.
3. A key process parameter (KPP) affects process performance, such as yield or concentration, and has no effect on a CQA within its range.
4. A general process parameter (GPP) has no relevant effect on a CQA or on process performance within its range.

A significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical. The PCR-00N should state the size of the effect beside its significance and give the reason for each class. The classification at this revision counts `{python} cc.get("CPP", 0)` CPP, `{python} cc.get("WC-CPP", 0)` WC-CPP, `{python} cc.get("KPP", 0)` KPP and `{python} cc.get("GPP", 0)` GPP, and is consolidated in PCMR-001.

## Method for fragments {#sec-fragments}

From `{python} amd_date`, fragments are measured by nrCE-SDS (`{python} cesds_amv`, under `{python} cesds_sop`) in every study at every step. This follows the decision to change the fragment method to nrCE-SDS (`{python} amd_id`). One method across the train is needed because fragment results are compared across steps, and a comparison between two methods would mix method bias with step performance. Designs executed before that date measured fragments by SEC (@tbl-methods-by-study). The screening designs of `{python} sec_only_scr` and the invalidated first execution of the anion exchange design have SEC results only. The response-surface designs of `{python} ret_rsm` were measured by SEC, and their retained samples were later re-tested by nrCE-SDS. The cation exchange response-surface design ran across the decision date and measured fragments by both methods on every run.

The decision followed the comparability study S-CEX-FRC (`{python} frc_start` to `{python} frc_end`), in which SEC (`{python} sec_amv`) and nrCE-SDS were run on the same samples. SEC read fragments high wherever the sample still carried host cell protein, because the part of the host cell protein that elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC is counted as fragment. The excess can never exceed the host cell protein present. It was a few tenths of a percent in the Protein A and viral inactivation pools and close to zero from the cation exchange pool onward. From the cation exchange pool onward the two methods agreed (INV-001 finding 6). SEC remains the method for aggregate (HMW), where no such interference applies.

@tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in which study. Retained response-surface samples of Protein A and low-pH viral inactivation were re-tested by nrCE-SDS between `{python} pa_ret_start` and `{python} pa_ret_end`. Screening samples were not retained. Their SEC fragment results are kept in the record but are not used for any decision. The re-executed anion exchange design ran after the decision and measured fragments by nrCE-SDS.


## Capability and the probability of an out-of-specification drug substance {#sec-acc-capability}

Capability is estimated as in @sec-capability and judged for each CQA in PCMR-001 against two values.

1. A Cpk of at least `{python} cpk_target` is expected of a CQA in routine manufacture. At that value the nearest limit lies `{python} cpk_sigma` standard deviations from the process mean, and a normal process would put about `{python} cpk_ppm` batches per million beyond that limit.
2. A CQA with a Cpk below `{python} cpk_min` needs an action in the control strategy. At that value the process spread, at three standard deviations on the limiting side, just reaches the criterion. The action may be a tighter NOR, an added in-process control or added testing. PCMR-001 should name the action.

A Cpk between the two values is acceptable. PCMR-001 should then state the side of the criterion that limits it and the parameters that drive it. For the probability of an out-of-specification drug substance, PCMR-001 should report the count of simulated batches outside each criterion and the tail probability, and should discuss every attribute with a simulated batch outside its criterion.

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The campaign delivers the following documents.

1. One PCP-00N and one PCR-00N for each of the `{python} n_steps` steps, each report paired with its plan.
2. PCMR-001, which consolidates the reports into the design spaces, the PARs, the parameter classes, the capability of the drug substance and the control strategy.
3. A ground-truth annex for each controlled document, built from the same data as the document.

In Version 1.0 each step plan was approved before the first characterization run of its step, and each report after the data of all its studies were complete. PCMR-001 is written last.

@tbl-chronology records the execution window of every study, in order of start. The campaign ran from `{python} first_start` to `{python} last_end` across `{python} n_studies` studies. Some steps were studied in parallel, because their scale-down models are independent of each other. The first execution of the anion exchange design (S-AEX-SUP) was invalidated under deviation DEV-008-01, because its load material had been deamidated during an extended hold after neutralization and did not represent the process. The design was re-executed as S-AEX-SCR and S-AEX-RSM.
